stories.notes: Multi-platform live preview is a complex feature with real-time rendering, state synchronization, and cross-platform (GO, UP, MX) concerns. No acceptance criteria exist yet (empty array, null spec). Openspec runs first to elaborate requirements and define AC; speckit follows to harden testability, security, and edge cases.

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a novel capability — no existing code handles real-time CMS preview updates. The attachment point is useContent (236 callers) because it is the single choke point for content delivery. Integrating Live Preview there propagates updates to all consumers without individual component changes. VCs are derived solely from the description since ACs are empty, and stop at the Contentstack boundary by asserting behavior given mocked preview events.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array, so all criteria above are new. I derived them from the story title/description (Live Preview of Content in CMS), the four key files (useContent.ts as the propagation choke point, contentstack.ts as the CMS service layer, contentCard.ts as the primary content interface, ContentstackLink.tsx as a concrete consumer), and openspec's note about useContent being the single choke point for 236 callers. Key design decisions: AC-1/AC-3 establish the core happy-path preview behavior; AC-2 ensures zero regression in production; AC-4 addresses render efficiency; AC-5/AC-9 cover error/resilience cases (connection failure, malformed data); AC-6 covers resource cleanup; AC-7/AC-8/AC-12 tie preview updates to the specific content shapes and components named in the technical notes; AC-10 enforces cross-codebase parity (GO, UP, MX); AC-11 addresses the edge case of rapid-fire preview events. CAVEAT: Without reading the actual file contents, I cannot assert specifics about Contentstack's Live Preview SDK API surface, the exact shape of preview event payloads, or the current signature of useContent. These ACs are intentionally framed as observable outcomes independent of implementation so they remain valid regardless, but the exact test assertions may need tightening once the Contentstack Live Preview documentation and current code are consulted.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: All four manifest paths exist (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx) — no missing files. Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: openspec identified the architectural choke point (useContent as the single propagation hub for 236 callers) and defined the integration strategy; speckit derived 12 verification criteria spanning happy path, production regression, render efficiency, error resilience, resource cleanup, cross-platform parity (GO/UP/MX), and rapid-fire event edge cases. These contributions are complementary. However, speckit explicitly caveats that it did not read actual file contents and cannot assert specifics about Contentstack's Live Preview SDK API surface, preview event payload shapes, or the current useContent signature. For a complex real-time, multi-platform feature, this gap is significant: the VCs are framed as observable outcomes to remain implementation-agnostic, which is a reasonable mitigation, but the exact test assertions may need tightening against real code and SDK documentation before implementation. Human review should validate that the verification criteria are concretely testable given the actual Contentstack Live Preview API and current useContent signature, and confirm that the four-file scope is sufficient (e.g., no missing WebSocket or real-time subscription layer file).
